correctness.rationale: Independently factor K=L diag(I,-S)L^T, with L having lower-left block A and identity diagonal. Then B=L diag(I,Pi)L^{-1}; B is idempotent, with rank n+rank(Pi), so singular precisely for a nontrivial omission. On the image of the zero-start Krylov space every positive order fits only the line through B(b,0), giving t=E/(E+R²) and the stated squared residual. K is invertible, so ker(B)=ker(the inverse application) and the original-variable reconstruction is independent of any nonuniqueness in the transformed iterate. Applying the inverse application to t(b,0) gives x_G=t Pi x_*; Parseval gives the error identity. In an omitted Fourier mode the range line is (1,a_j), giving the stated floor. The two-mode rational witness gives 4/3 versus 4/5 and squared error 1/9+4/25=61/225. Strictness is possible, not universal; for example both floors vanish for R=0. Attenuation affects nonzero retained components when R>0. The result concerns mathematical Krylov minima, not iterates executable after breakdown.
